rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Râzî says God alone truly takes souls, while angels perform delegated tasks; other verses attribute the taking to angels by agency, while this one attributes it to God in reality.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî tefsirinde buna şöyle bir cevap verilmiştir: “Hakikatte teveffî eden ancak Allah teâlâ’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı accepts Râzî’s account but stresses that this verse describes the instant of return to God, a more important nuance than the general attribution of death to God through angels.
rows.anchor: Buradaki teveffî o ircâ‘ve red lahzasını beyandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Angel of Death takes the bodily life called the animal soul, whereas God directly takes the rational soul, the human spirit breathed by the Lord.
rows.anchor: denilen hayât-ı cismâniye rûhunu kabzeder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses saying people are returned to God after death indicate that the rational soul’s taking is uniquely and directly God’s act.
rows.anchor: ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ [es-Secde 32/11] buyurulması da bu ihtisâsı iş‘âr eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking, withholding, and releasing souls point to God’s sole divinity, final return, resurrection and judgment, and the contrasting fates of disbelievers and the faithful; he links this to the declaration that we belong to God and return to Him.
rows.anchor: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ [el-Bakara 2/156] mısdâkına delâlet ederler

rows.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: To answer whether sleep-like separation of the soul would spare disbelievers the experience of punishment, the author reports al-Kashshāf’s view that the rational soul is not subject to death.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf bu suâle meydan vermemek için

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: Elmalılı gives as the real answer a couplet attributed to Ali: if the dead were simply left, death would be rest, but they are resurrected and questioned about everything.
rows.anchor: asıl cevâbı Hazret-i Ali’ye nisbet olunan şu kıtadadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s absolute control over taking, retaining, and releasing souls shows that this restraint is a detention for resurrection, not an escape; one should reflect on the awe, majesty, and beauty of meeting God.
rows.anchor: bu habs ü imsâkin onları kaçırmayıp ba‘s için bir habs ü tevkif olduğunu istintac etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the trumpet blast, disbelievers will ask who raised them from their resting place, which clarifies this point about detention for resurrection.
rows.anchor: Yâsîn’de geçtiği üzere Sûr nefh olununca kâfirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the same reason, disbelievers will say that God caused them to die twice and live twice.
rows.anchor: Ve yine bundan dolayıdır ki kâfirler

words: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ شُفَعَآءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists’ recourse against the warnings is to claim intercessors: they say they worship idols only to draw near to God and claim that God has taken a son.
rows.anchor: müşriklerin yegâne tutundukları tutamak şefaat davası olduğu için buyuruluyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assertion that the idols own nothing and have no understanding first refutes the claim that they can intercede.
rows.anchor: bu evvelâ putların şefaati davasını ibtaldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All intercession belongs to God; nobody may intercede before Him without His permission, and those permitted to intercede seek His pleasure.
rows.anchor: Bütün şefaat Allah içindir. Onun da mâliki O’dur. O’nun izni olmaksızın huzûrunda kimse şefaat edemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s threat is an example of the earlier statement that every community plotted against its messenger.
rows.anchor: kavline bir misâl gösterilmiş de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ miracles had broken Pharaoh’s despotism: he was confused and could no longer do as he wished.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Mûsâ’nın mu‘cizâtı karşısında Firavun’un istibdâdı kırılmış, dilediğini yapamaz olmuş ve şaşırmıştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account in al-Aʿrāf suggests the matter had moved beyond consulting the public to an intervention, prompting Pharaoh to shout that they should let him act.
rows.anchor: mesele cemiyetin yalnız re’yine müracaattan ibaret kalmamış, bir müdahale mâhiyetini almış olmalı ki “bırakın beni” diye bağırıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh tries to deny or mock God by saying Moses should call on his Lord, yet presents himself as pious by warning that Moses will change their religion.
rows.anchor: bir taraftan da “dininizi değiştirecek” diye dindarlık gösteriyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı speculates that the God Pharaoh calls his own may be his sovereignty.
rows.anchor: Belki onun Allah dediği kendi saltanatıdır.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some took the believing man from Pharaoh’s family to be an Israelite, a view Elmalılı does not accept as the phrase’s apparent sense.
rows.anchor: bazıları bu zâtın İsrâilîlerden olduğunu zannetmişlerse de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of being from Pharaoh’s household points instead to an Egyptian, perhaps a member of Pharaoh’s own dynasty.
rows.anchor: vasfının zâhiri bunun daha ziyade Mısırlılardan ve belki Firavun’un kendi hânedânından olduğunu anlatıyor

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: Al-Suddī relates that the believer was Pharaoh’s cousin.
rows.anchor: Süddî bunu Firavun’un amcası oğlu diye rivayet eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported identification makes the believer heir apparent and head of the police.
rows.anchor: Veliyy-i ahdi ve sâhib-şurtası, yani polis nâzırı olduğu da söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God especially recounts this man’s speeches and struggle against Pharaoh and his family, the sūra is named Sūrat al-Muʾmin after him.
rows.anchor: bu sûreye onun nâmına muzâf olarak “Sûre-i Mü’min” denilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He concealed his faith and used secret stratagems to keep Pharaoh at bay for a time; when Moses’ execution was decided, he came forward, beginning with gradual counsel and then open opposition.
rows.anchor: evvelâ tedric ile nasihate başlamış

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At first he speaks cautiously without revealing his faith, arguing from the injustice of killing a man for saying that his Lord is God and from the proofs Moses had brought.
rows.anchor: Bir adamı “Rabbim Allah” diyor diye öldürecek misiniz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses is lying, the lie and its consequence fall on him, so there is no need to kill him before his falsehood is established.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh yalancılığı tahakkuk etmeden öldürmeye ihtiyâcınız yok

words: وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًۭا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses is truthful, at least some of his threatened punishment will befall them, even in this world if they reject the afterlife.
rows.anchor: âhirete inanmıyorsanız dünyada azâbı gelir

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One inference is that if Moses were an extreme liar, God would not have given him clear signs or supported him with miracles.
rows.anchor: o aşırı bir yalancı olsa idi Allah ona o beyyineleri vermez, o mucizelerle teyid eylemezdi

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other inference is that a truly profligate liar would not succeed, so there is no need to strive to kill him.
rows.anchor: şüphe yoktur, öldüreceğiz diye uğraşmaya

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both arguments indirectly target Pharaoh: as a blood-shedding profligate liar, God will not help him kill Moses, and Pharaoh will only bring harm on himself.
rows.anchor: asıl maksad da Firavun’a târizdir. Yani sen bu kadar kan döken müsrif bir yalancısın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer’s direct address to his people shows the speeches took place before a public council rather than in a private gathering.
rows.anchor: doğrudan doğru kavme hitap etmesinden anlaşılıyor ki bu hatâbeler husûsî bir mecliste değil, umûmî bir şûrâda cereyan etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s claim that he only shows them his own view means he is expressing an opinion, not issuing a direct order to execute Moses.
rows.anchor: Firavun bu kelâmıyla yalnız re’yini anlatmış oluyor, doğrudan doğru icrâ emri veremiyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-Tanād means the day of calling or crying out, a name for resurrection because people call for help, or the people of Paradise and Hell call to one another as in 7:44.
rows.anchor: tenâdî günü, çığırışma, bağırışma günü demektir ki kıyamet gününün bir ismidir

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some identify this Joseph as Joseph son of Ephraim, grandson of the earlier Joseph.
rows.anchor: Bazıları buradaki Yûsuf’tan murad, Hazret-i Yûsuf’un torunu Yûsuf b. Efrâyim b. Yûsuf demişlerse de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the correct identification is Joseph son of Jacob.
rows.anchor: doğrusu Yûsuf b. Ya‘kūb aleyhisselâm’dır

rows.speaker: Tefsîr-i Kurtubî
rows.claim: As reported in al-Qurṭubī, the Pharaoh of Moses was not the Pharaoh of Joseph: Joseph’s Pharaoh was Amalekite, whereas Moses’ was Coptic.
rows.anchor: Tefsîr-i Kurtubî’de mezkur olduğu üzere Hazret-i Mûsâ’nın Firavunu Hazret-i Yûsuf’un Firavunu değildir

words: مَنْ عَمِلَ سَيِّئَةًۭ فَلَا يُجْزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Justice gives a wrongdoer no more than an equivalent evil; evil cannot merit a good reward, and punishment cannot exceed the wrong done.
rows.anchor: Şu kadar ki yaptığı kötülükten fazla değil, onun misli bir kötülüktür

words: مَنْ عَمِلَ سَيِّئَةًۭ فَلَا يُجْزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some wrongdoers may be forgiven wholly or partly, but forgiveness is an additional grace rather than the punishment due for that wrong.
rows.anchor: Fakat afv, o kötülüğün cezâsı değil, başkaca bir fazldır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good deeds merit good in return; although justice would require an equal measure, divine beneficence can multiply the reward tenfold or without limit, like a seed producing ten, one hundred, or seven hundred grains.
rows.anchor: ihsan kanunu, onun on mislinden hesapsız emsâline kadar çıkar; yerine iyi bir dâne eken, on dâne alabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer’s appeal against Pharaoh describes his resistance and invitation as a lawful, certain matter of deliverance, not rebellion.
rows.anchor: Bu hitap da Firavun’a karşı yapılan bu hurûc ve davetin bir bağy olmayıp meşrû ve muhakkak bir necat meselesi olduğunu beyandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protected the believer and his companions from Pharaoh’s family’s evil plots: they neither fell into their opponents’ evil deeds nor were harmed by the pursuit, while the worst punishment overtook Pharaoh’s family.
rows.anchor: Onlar âl-i Firavun’un düştükleri kötü amellere düşmedikleri gibi âl-i Firavun’un onlar hakkında kurdukları fena tuzaklara da düşmediler

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the soldiers Pharaoh sent to pursue the believer perished, and that Pharaoh and his troops were later drowned.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayete göre Firavun’un onu tâkip için gönderdiği asker telef olmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı parses Fire as the subject and the following clause, saying they are exposed to it morning and evening, as its predicate.
rows.anchor: Ateş mübtedâdır, haberi şu: يُعْرَضُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s family were destroyed by punishment in this life and are exposed to the Fire morning and evening in the intermediate state until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: âhirete kadar âlem-i berzahta da akşam sabah nâra arz ile ta‘zîb olunmaktadırlar
